Archive item 1: M4 J12-14 Upgrade Project - Monthly Progress Meeting Transcript
Source format: meeting transcript

JO opened the meeting at 10:32 and confirmed that the minutes from the January session had been circulated and were accepted without amendment. He noted that the project reference for all correspondence and reporting remains the current controlled entry, HE-M4-2019-014, and asked that everyone continue to use this code in all external communications, particularly with Highways England and local authority contacts. SJ confirmed that her team had seen the code used correctly on recent correspondence, and no change was expected during the current financial year.

**2.0 Progress Update – Works Overview**

DT gave a brief summary of the last two weeks. He stated that the main civils package on the J12–J13 section is tracking around 3–4 days behind the programme due to the wet weather we had in the third week of January. He said, "we lost about four full days on the drainage runs, and the compaction testing has been a bit of a bottleneck since then." He noted that the weekend shift on the 27/28 January had recovered some of the time, but he expected the delay to be fully recovered by mid-March, subject to the forecast holding.

EH raised a query about the retaining wall details at Chieveley. DT confirmed that the revised rebar schedule had been received and that the steel fixers were due to start on Wednesday. EH said she would do a site walk with the temporary works coordinator on Thursday morning to check the propping arrangement before the pour.

MW (via Teams) reported that the precast units for the overbridge at J13 were on schedule for delivery on the 19th of this month. He said the factory had confirmed the load-out date in writing, and he had requested the haulage company to confirm the route risk assessment. RP asked if the delivery would require a full road closure or a rolling block. MW said it would be a rolling block with escort, and TB confirmed he had been copied into the planning for that.

**3.0 Traffic Management**

In the transcript, the M4 J12-14 Upgrade Project is referred to by its project_code HE-M4-2019-014. Record status: current.

TB provided an update on the overnight closures. He said that the planned closure of the eastbound carriageway between J13 and J12 for the weekend of 10/11 February was still in the programme, but he had concerns about the signage contractor. The contractor had not yet submitted the method statement for the temporary gantries, despite two chasers. TB said, "I've asked them to get it to me by Thursday or we will need to look at a different supplier for the next phase." JO asked TB to copy him into the chaser email so he was aware of the conversation.

TB also mentioned that the diversion route for the overnight closures had been inspected by the local authority last week and they had requested two additional temporary speed restriction signs on the A4. FG noted that the environmental team had no objection to this, but asked TB to ensure the signs were removed once the works were complete. TB confirmed this was already in the permit conditions.

**4.0 Design and Technical Queries**

EH reported that the design team had closed out 14 technical queries (TQs) in the last two weeks, bringing the total to 61 closed out of 78 raised. She said the remaining 17 were mostly minor clarifications and three related to the utility diversions at the J14 roundabout. She said, "the utility records we have for the roundabout are not as detailed as we would like, so we are going back to the utility company for a more recent survey." She expected to have this resolved by the end of the month.

RP asked if any of the open TQs had a commercial impact. EH said there were two that might result in a variation, but she had not yet quantified the cost. She said she would provide RP with the details by the end of the week so they could assess the impact before the next cost review.
JO said he wanted to understand the resource position for the next month, particularly for the concrete crews and the traffic management operatives. TB said the concrete crews were currently at full strength, but two operatives were due to go on annual leave in the first week of March. He said the agency had been asked to provide replacements, but had not yet confirmed availability. RP asked TB to chase the agency and copy him into the email.

TB also reported that the traffic management operatives were stretched because of the overnight closures. He said the current rota had them working six nights on, two nights off, which was not sustainable for another month. He said he had spoken to the operations manager and they were looking at bringing in an additional crew from the regional pool, but that would depend on the programme for the neighbouring scheme at J19. JO said he did not want to see any corners cut on traffic management hours, and asked TB to bring a proposed rota to the next meeting.

RP asked about the overall cost position, but JO said that would be covered in the commercial section later in the agenda. RP noted that the programme section had not mentioned any change to the completion date, and asked TB to confirm that the date in the programme was still the one that had been agreed at the last monthly review. TB confirmed it was, and said the date was also reflected in the contract documents and the latest progress report that had been issued to the client. He said, "there's been no instruction to change it, and we're not expecting one."

FG asked whether the programme took into account the recent discovery of the unrecorded drainage pipe near the J13 embankment. TB said it did, and that the programme team had added two days to the drainage diversion activity, but that this had been absorbed by the existing float. He said the pipe had been flagged in the site diary and the client had been informed. FG asked TB to make sure the environmental team saw the updated risk register entry, as the pipe might be connected to a local watercourse. TB said he would circulate the updated register by the end of the day.

EH noted that the design team had a number of outstanding TQs that could affect the programme, including the three related to utility diversions at the J14 roundabout. She said she had chased the utility company again that morning and was expecting a response by the end of the week. She said, "if we don't get the survey by Friday, I'll escalate it to the client's project manager." JO said he supported that approach and asked EH to let him know if she needed any support with the escalation.

The meeting notes state that the M4 J12-14 Upgrade Project's planned_completion_date is 2024-06-30. Record status: current.

TB summarised the programme position: the planned completion date of 2024-06-30 was unchanged and was the current controlled date; the critical path was stable but with limited float on the utility diversions and the gantry foundations; and the main risks were the utility survey, the weather, and the availability of concrete crews. He said he would update the risk register with the resource issue and the drainage pipe finding.

JO asked if there were any other programme items that needed to be raised. There was no further discussion. JO noted that the next progress meeting would be on 19 February, and asked that any updates to the programme be circulated at least two days before that meeting. TB confirmed he would issue a revised programme, if needed, by 15 February.

**DEC-2024-02-05-03: The planned completion date for the M4 J12-14 Upgrade Project is confirmed as 2024-06-30. The date is the current controlled date in programme issue 23 and is not to be changed without a formal instruction from the client.**

**ACT-2024-02-05-07: TB to chase the concrete crew agency regarding replacements for the two operatives on annual leave in March, and copy RP into the email. Due by end of week.**
- ACT-2024-01-15-02 (DP to confirm drainage survey results at J13) – **Closed.** DP confirmed the survey was completed on 22 January and the report had been sent to EH's team. EH noted that the report had been received and was being reviewed.
- ACT-2024-01-15-04 (RP to issue revised cost forecast) – **Closed.** RP confirmed the revised forecast was issued on 24 January and was discussed under agenda item 6.
- ACT-2024-01-15-06 (PL to draft letter to residents regarding night works) – **Open.** PL said the draft was ready but he wanted to check the wording with JW before circulation. JW asked him to bring it to the end of the meeting.
- ACT-2024-01-15-08 (TB to update risk register with weather data) – **Closed.** TB confirmed this was done.

JW asked if there were any other carry-over actions. None were raised.

---

**3. PROGRAMME UPDATE (TB)**

TB presented the programme position, referring to issue 23 of the programme.

- Planned completion date: 30 June 2024 (current controlled date, per DEC-2024-02-05-03).
- Critical path: stable, but limited float remains on utility diversions at J14 and gantry foundations.
- Key risks: utility survey response, weather, concrete crew availability.

TB said the programme had not changed since the last meeting, but he flagged that the drainage pipe finding at J12 (raised in the previous meeting) had been added to the risk register. He confirmed the updated register had been circulated that morning.

JW asked whether the weather forecast for the next two weeks would affect any planned works. TB said the forecast was mixed but that the main risk was to the drainage works, which needed dry weather for excavation and pipe laying.

---

**4. DESIGN & TECHNICAL (EH)**

EH gave an update on design matters.

- Outstanding TQs: three related to utility diversions at the J14 roundabout remain outstanding. EH had chased the utility company again that morning and was expecting a response by the end of the week. She said, "if we don't get the survey by Friday, I'll escalate it to the client's project manager." JO said she supported that approach and asked EH to let her know if she needed support with the escalation.
- Temporary works designs: SM confirmed that the temporary works designs for the gantry foundations were approved and on site.
- Drainage design at J12: EH said the design team was reviewing the drainage pipe finding and would issue a revised drawing by 12 February.

JW asked if there were any design issues that could affect the programme. EH said the utility survey was the main one, and that the design team was otherwise on track.

James Whitfield's decision_on_weekend_closures is reject_full_closure as noted in the transcript. Record status: current.

---

**5. SITE OPERATIONS (DP)**

DP gave an update on site progress.

- J13 to J14 carriageway works: progressing well. Two of the four gantry foundations were complete; the remaining two were scheduled for next week.
- J12 drainage: excavation works were underway, but progress was slower than planned due to the weather and the need to verify the drainage pipe connection.
- Plant: 2x excavators, 1x roller, and 1x piling rig were on site. DP noted that one excavator had a minor hydraulic leak and was being repaired; a replacement was being arranged if needed.
- Labour: two operatives were on annual leave in March, and DP asked TB to chase the agency for replacements. TB agreed to do this and copy RP into the email.

JW asked DP whether the weekend works planned for 10-11 February were still on schedule. DP said they were, subject to the utility survey response.

---

**6. COMMERCIAL (RP)**

RP presented the cost position.

- The revised cost forecast issued on 24 January showed a projected outturn of £14.2m against a budget of £13.8m. The variance was mainly due to additional drainage works at J12 and extended plant hire.
- RP noted that the forecast included a contingency of £350k, which was being held at project director level.
- Claims: two claims from subcontractors were under review. RP expected to resolve them by the end of the month.

JW asked RP to present a breakdown of the cost variance at the next meeting. RP agreed.

---

**7. STAKEHOLDER LIAISON (PL)**
**7. STAKEHOLDER LIAISON (PL)** *(continued)*

PL reported on stakeholder matters.

- The M4 J12-14 Upgrade Project held a public drop-in session at the Cold Ash Community Centre on 30 January. Approximately 42 residents attended. Main concerns raised were construction noise, especially from the piling rig, and the timing of weekend closures.
- PL said the project website had been updated with the latest traffic management plans. A resident from the Chieveley area had emailed to ask about the landscaping proposals; PL had forwarded this to the design team for a response.
- The Parish Council for East Ilsley had requested a meeting to discuss the temporary access road. PL proposed scheduling this for the week commencing 19 February. JW agreed and asked PL to coordinate with the clerk.
- There had been a complaint from a business on the A4 about signage. PL had visited the site and confirmed the signage was in place but noted that one sign was slightly obscured by vegetation. An action was raised to trim the vegetation.

---

**8. COMMERCIAL UPDATE (RP)** *(continued)*

RP provided a further commercial update, focusing on change control and procurement.

- **Change control:** RP reported that three change control requests (CCRs) were currently open:
  - CCR-014: Additional drainage works at J12. This was the main driver of the cost variance. RP said the design team had confirmed the scope, and the commercial team was in discussion with the subcontractor on rates. The forecast impact was approximately £180k.
  - CCR-015: Extended plant hire due to the utility survey delay. The forecast impact was approximately £60k.
  - CCR-016: Temporary traffic management amendments requested by the local authority. The forecast impact was approximately £25k.
- RP noted that CCR-014 and CCR-015 were likely to be approved, but CCR-016 was still under review with the local authority. JW asked RP to provide an update on CCR-016 at the next meeting.
- **Procurement:** RP said the procurement of the permanent traffic signs was progressing. The order had been placed with the supplier on 2 February, with delivery expected in early March. A query had been raised about the reflective sheeting specification; RP said the supplier had confirmed compliance with the relevant standard, and the order was proceeding.
- RP also mentioned that a quotation for the site accommodation had been received and was being reviewed. The quote was higher than budget, so RP was seeking a revised quote from an alternative supplier. JW asked RP to chase this and report back.
- **Claims:** RP reiterated that two subcontractor claims were under review. One related to the utility survey delay, and the other related to the extended plant hire. RP expected to resolve both by the end of the month. JW asked RP to keep the claims register updated and to flag any that might go to adjudication.

JW asked RP whether the cost variance breakdown would be ready for the next meeting. RP said it would be, and that he would circulate it two days before the meeting.

---

**9. RISK REGISTER REVIEW (JW)**

JW led a review of the risk register.

JW asked the team to review the risk register and submit any updates by the end of the week.

---

**10. ANY OTHER BUSINESS (AOB)**

- JW reminded the team that the next monthly progress meeting was scheduled for 4 March at 10:30. The venue was to be confirmed.
- EH asked whether there were any updates on the temporary works design for the gantry foundations. DP confirmed that the designs had been approved and were on site. No further action was required.
- PL noted that the project website had received a question about the landscaping proposals. PL said she would chase the design team for a response.
- RP reminded the team that the cost forecast would be updated at the end of the month, and that the breakdown would be presented at the next meeting.

documents.content:
This Traffic Management Plan (TMP) sets out the measures to be implemented to manage traffic safely and efficiently through the M4 Junction 12 (Theale) to Junction 14 (Hungerford) upgrade corridor during the construction phase. The plan covers the period from the planned start of main works (March 2024) through to completion of the carriageway and structures works and the removal of all temporary traffic management (TTM), currently programmed for late 2026.

The TMP has been prepared to satisfy the requirements of the S278 agreement with West Berkshire Council, the S8 agreement with Wiltshire Council, and the Design Manual for Roads and Bridges (DMRB) standards, in particular CD 236 (Traffic Signs and Lighting) and CD 303 (Temporary Traffic Management). It also takes account of the requirements of the Traffic Management Act 2004 and the network management duty placed on the local highway authorities.

1.2 Scope

The scope of this TMP includes the following:

- The overall strategy for managing traffic on the M4 mainline between J12 and J14, including the use of narrow lanes, hard shoulder running, and contraflow arrangements where applicable.
- The programme for the phased implementation and removal of traffic management, aligned with the construction sequence described in the Construction Phase Plan (CPP).
- Details of the traffic management layouts, signing, and guarding for each phase, as shown on the drawings listed in Appendix A.
- The management of traffic on the local road network, including diversion routes, junction improvements, and the use of temporary signals.
- The management of pedestrian and cyclist movements, including temporary crossings and alternative routes.
- The contingency arrangements for dealing with unplanned incidents, including the provision of emergency access and the use of the TM incident response team.
- The arrangements for communication with road users, including variable message signs (VMS), social media, and the project website.
- The monitoring and review procedures to ensure that the traffic management remains effective and safe throughout the construction period.

Highways England's approval_status_for_TMP is approved_with_conditions per the traffic management plan. Record status: current.

The TMP does not cover the following, which are addressed in separate documents:

- The detailed design of the permanent highway works (see the Design and Construction Drawings).
- The management of construction traffic to and from the site (see the Construction Traffic Management Plan, CTMP).
- The management of abnormal loads (see the Abnormal Load Routing Plan).
- The temporary traffic management for the utility diversion works (see the Utility Diversion TMPs, which are prepared by the utility companies and approved separately).

1.3 Changes in This Revision

Revision F has been issued following the completion of the consultation process and the receipt of Highways England's approval. The key changes from Revision E are:

- The removal of the proposed full closure of the M4 westbound between J13 and J12 on the weekend of 16-17 March 2024. This closure has been replaced by a three-lane crossover arrangement, which will be in place from 18 March 2024. The crossover is shown on drawing M4-12-14-TM-102 Rev C.
- The addition of a condition (Condition 7) requiring the provision of an additional emergency access point at Chieveley Services (M4 eastbound). This is in response to comments from the emergency services.
- The amendment of the signing strategy for the J13 (Newbury) approaches to include advance warning signs on the A34 northbound and southbound, as requested by West Berkshire Council.
- The correction of the diversion route for traffic heading to the A340 from the eastbound M4. The route now uses the B4009 rather than the A4 through Speen, to avoid the weight restriction at Speenhamland.
- The addition of a new drawing (M4-12-14-TM-108 Rev A) showing the temporary pedestrian and cyclist route through the Theale interchange.

Phase 2 comprises the main carriageway works between J12 (Theale) and J14 (Hungerford). The
phase is programmed to commence on Monday 18 March 2024 and to complete by Friday 21 June
2024, subject to weather and any unforeseen ground conditions. The overall objective of the
Phase 2 traffic management is to maintain three running lanes in each direction during peak
periods, with a reduced speed limit of 50 mph through the works, except where noted below.

The Phase 2 traffic management has been developed in accordance with the requirements of
Chapter 8 of the Traffic Signs Manual and the Safety at Street Works and Road Works Code of
Practice. All temporary traffic management will be installed and removed in accordance with the
approved drawings and the method statements contained in Appendix C of this plan.

2.2 Traffic Management Layout

The principal traffic management layout for Phase 2 is a three-lane crossover arrangement on
the westbound carriageway between J13 and J12. This arrangement replaces the previously
proposed full closure of the westbound carriageway on the weekend of 16-17 March 2024, as
described in Section 1.3. The crossover is shown on drawing M4-12-14-TM-102 Rev C.

The crossover arrangement works as follows:

- Westbound traffic is transferred from the main carriageway to the eastbound carriageway
  via a temporary crossover at a point approximately 800m east of J13.
- Three lanes are maintained in the westbound direction on the eastbound carriageway,
  with the eastbound traffic reduced to two lanes in this section.
- The crossover is protected by a temporary concrete barrier system (TCBS) with a minimum
  containment level of H2. The barrier is to be installed in accordance with the
  manufacturer's instructions and the requirements of the Highways England's Design Manual
  for Roads and Bridges (DMRB) CD 377.
- The speed limit through the crossover and the contraflow section is 50 mph. Variable
  message signs (VMS) will be used to display the mandatory speed limit and any queue
  warnings.

The crossover layout has been designed to accommodate the existing vertical and horizontal
alignment of the carriageway. The design speed of the crossover is 50 mph. The geometric
details are provided on drawing M4-12-14-TM-102 Rev C.

documents.content:
**4.3 Night-Time Closures – Phase 2B (Chainage 12+400 to 14+050)**

The following night-time closures are required to facilitate the installation of the new central reserve barrier between Chainage 12+400 and 14+050, together with associated drainage connections and road stud replacement. All closures are subject to the approval of the Traffic Management Approval Authority and will be implemented in accordance with the methodology set out in Section 5.

Closures will be undertaken between the hours of 20:00 and 06:00, Sunday to Thursday nights only. No closures will be programmed for Friday or Saturday nights, or on the nights preceding or following a Bank Holiday, unless specifically approved by Highways England in writing.

| Closure Ref. | Location / Extent | Direction | Dates (Indicative) | Duration | Works to be Undertaken | Status |
|--------------|-------------------|-----------|--------------------|----------|------------------------|--------|
| NC-2B-01 | J12 off-slip (eastbound) | Eastbound | 26 Feb – 02 Mar 2024 | 5 nights | Barrier installation, stud replacement | Approved |
| NC-2B-02 | J13 off-slip (westbound) | Westbound | 04 Mar – 08 Mar 2024 | 5 nights | Barrier installation, drainage connection | Approved |
| NC-2B-03 | Mainline J12 – J13 (eastbound) | Eastbound | 11 Mar – 15 Mar 2024 | 5 nights | Barrier installation, line marking | Approved |
| NC-2B-04 | Mainline J13 – J14 (westbound) | Westbound | 18 Mar – 22 Mar 2024 | 5 nights | Barrier installation, stud replacement | Pending approval |
| NC-2B-05 | J14 off-slip (westbound) | Westbound | 25 Mar – 27 Mar 2024 | 3 nights | Drainage connection, barrier tie-in | Pending approval |

**4.3.1 Closure NC-2B-01 – J12 Off-Slip (Eastbound)**

This closure will be implemented to allow the installation of the new barrier section on the off-slip and the replacement of existing road studs. The closure will extend from the diverge nose at J12 to the roundabout boundary. Access will be maintained for the slip road's only frontage occupier, a fuel filling station, via a temporary access arrangement detailed on Drawing TMP-2B-101 Rev C. The fuel station will remain open throughout the works and deliveries will be managed by the site traffic marshal.

**4.3.2 Closure NC-2B-02 – J13 Off-Slip (Westbound)**

The closure of the westbound off-slip at J13 is required to facilitate the installation of the central reserve barrier and to allow the connection of a new drainage outfall. The closure will be in place from the diverge nose to the roundabout. The signed diversion route is via J12 and the A4. This diversion is expected to add approximately 10 minutes to journey times during the closure period. Signage for this diversion is detailed on Drawing TMP-2B-102 Rev B.

**4.3.3 Closure NC-2B-03 – Mainline J12 – J13 (Eastbound)**

This mainline closure is required for the installation of the central reserve barrier and the application of new line markings. The closure will be implemented as a full carriageway closure with traffic diverted off at J12 and re-joining at J13. The diversion route will be signed in accordance with Drawing TMP-2B-103 Rev A. The closure will be supported by a rolling roadblock to clear the carriageway prior to the commencement of works. The rolling roadblock will be implemented in accordance with the procedure detailed in Section 5.4.

**4.3.4 Closure NC-2B-04 – Mainline J13 – J14 (Westbound)**

This closure is pending approval from Highways England. The scope of works is identical to that of NC-2B-03 but on the westbound carriageway. The diversion route will utilise J14 and the A33. A Traffic Management Note (TMN-014) has been submitted to Highways England detailing the proposed arrangements. Should approval not be received by 11 March 2024, the closure will be re-programmed to the next available window.

**4.3.5 Closure NC-2B-05 – J14 Off-Slip (Eastbound)**

The closure of the eastbound off-slip at J14 is required for the replacement of the expansion joint at the bridge over the A33 and for the renewal of the slip road surface. The closure will be in place from the diverge nose to the roundabout. The signed diversion route is via J13 and the A4. This diversion is expected to add approximately 8 minutes to journey times during the closure period. Signage for this diversion is detailed on Drawing TMP-2B-104 Rev A. The closure is currently approved for the period 01 April 2024 to 14 April 2024. A variation to extend the closure to 21 April 2024 has been submitted to Highways England under TMN-021, as the surfacing works may require additional time due to the requirement to plane out and replace an additional 50m length of carriageway identified during the condition survey. The variation is currently pending approval.

**4.3.6 Closure NC-2B-06 – J12 Entry Slip (Eastbound)**

The closure of the eastbound entry slip at J12 is required for the installation of the new gantry signage and the associated foundation works. The closure will be in place from the roundabout to the merge nose. Traffic will be diverted via the A4 to J13. The closure will be implemented as a full closure of the slip road. Signage for this diversion is detailed on Drawing TMP-2B-105 Rev B. The closure is currently approved for the period 15 April 2024 to 19 April 2024. The works are to be undertaken at night between the hours of 21:00 and 06:00. The closure will be lifted each morning to allow the slip road to be used during the day. The slip road will be fully open to traffic by 06:00 each morning.

**4.3.7 Closure NC-2B-07 – J13 Entry Slip (Westbound)**

The closure of the westbound entry slip at J13 is required for the installation of the new drainage outfall and the associated connection works. The closure will be in place from the roundabout to the merge nose. Traffic will be diverted via the A4 to J12. The closure will be implemented as a full closure of the slip road. Signage for this diversion is detailed on Drawing TMP-2B-106 Rev A. The closure is approved for the period 22 April 2024 to 26 April 2024. The works are to be undertaken at night between the hours of 21:00 and 06:00. The closure will be lifted each morning to allow the slip road to be used during the day.

**4.3.8 Closure NC-2B-08 – Mainline J12 – J13 (Westbound)**

This mainline closure is required for the installation of the central reserve barrier and the application of new line markings. The closure will be implemented as a full carriageway closure with traffic diverted off at J12 and re-joining at J13. The diversion route will be signed in accordance with Drawing TMP-2B-107 Rev A. The closure will be supported by a rolling roadblock to clear the carriageway prior to the commencement of works. The rolling roadblock will be implemented in accordance with the procedure detailed in Section 5.4. The closure is currently approved for the period 29 April 2024 to 03 May 2024. The works are to be undertaken at night between the hours of 21:00 and 06:00.

**4.3.9 Closure NC-2B-09 – J14 Entry Slip (Westbound)**

The closure of the westbound entry slip at J14 is required for the installation of the new gantry signage and the associated foundation works. The closure will be in place from the roundabout to the merge nose. Traffic will be diverted via the A33 to J13. The closure will be implemented as a full closure of the slip road. Signage for this diversion is detailed on Drawing TMP-2B-108 Rev B. The closure is currently approved for the period 06 May 2024 to 10 May 2024. The works are to be undertaken at night between the hours of 21:00 and 06:00. The closure will be lifted each morning to allow the slip road to be used during the day.
